decision: done = /tools/exam-photo makes a JPG whose pixels, KB and format pass each preset's official rules, shows a check built by re-reading the output file, and per-exam pages exist

decision: v1 scope: presets + fit engine + stamp + check + per-exam pages; auto face crop and background whitening left out

decision: reuse bestJpegUnder search and the [landing] page pattern

decision: wrote 17 tests first with real JPEGs from the mozjpeg wasm codec in bun

decision: KB band = floor at 1024 B/KB, cap at 1000 B/KB
why: notices rarely say which KB they mean; this band passes under both

decision: files under the floor get padded with JPEG comment segments instead of fake detail
why: keeps pixels identical; portals reject small signatures at a 10-20 KB floor

decision: check re-parses the output JPEG header (SOF size, JFIF DPI) rather than trusting canvas settings
why: the check must reflect the file the user uploads

decision: studio is its own component on /tools/exam-photo, not a ToolWorkspace mode
why: one image per slot with live re-render on drag/zoom does not fit the pick-files, run, results flow

decision: signatures, thumbs and declarations are trimmed to the ink and fitted whole on white; only photos get drag/zoom framing
why: cropping a signature to fill the frame would cut strokes

decision: one page per exam at /exam-photo/<slug> with the rule table, source link and checked date, added to sitemap
why: people search these by exam name; dated source keeps the page honest

decision: specs test demands an official-domain source URL for every preset and output pixels inside the stated range
why: a wrong KB range costs someone their application; guard it in structure, not memory

decision: delegated official-spec research to a Sonnet subagent; spot-checked IBPS, SBI, CUET, JEE, NEET, SSC, RRB, UPSC numbers with pdftotext on the fetched PDFs
why: a wrong KB range costs someone their application; judge the worker's output against the source

decision: NEET finger/thumb set to 10-200 KB, not the subagent's 50-200 overlap

decision: dropped Agniveer; SSC and RRB presets are signature-only with a note that the photo is live-captured

decision: name/date stamp is an opt-in toggle, not tied to any preset

decision: UPSC uses IES/ISS 2026 sizes (photo 20-200, sign 20-100) and the older FAQ 350-1000 px bounds

decision: PAN uses Protean's guideline page: photo up to 20 KB, signature up to 10 KB, 200 DPI
why: Protean's articles say 50 KB; 20/10 passes both readings

decision: pad to floor + 2 KB (or band midpoint) instead of exactly the floor
why: browser run showed every IBPS file at exactly 20.0/10.0/50.0 KB, zero margin against strict rounding

decision: drag pans one-to-one with the pointer (scaled by crop size and free space), previews capped at 160 px, wide slots stack

decision: swept all 9 presets in the dev server with synthetic face and signature images

decision: phone width 375 px: no horizontal scroll, cards stack

decision: scoreboard row added under Only we have

decision: pixel and DPI rules can be minimum-only (RRB 140x60+, 100+ DPI); no invented 4000 px cap

decision: PAN pixels fixed at 197x276 and 354x157 (cm at 200 DPI); DPI wording conflict noted on page

decision: studio: error shown with no image, type check on drop, spinner stops on error, drag uses the area above the name band, other slots ignore name typing, shared file taken from handoff into the photo slot

decision: PAN 'lesser than 200 dpi' vs '200 DPI': we write exactly 200

decision: shared image goes to the photo slot only; on a signature-only exam a note offers 'Use as signature'

decision: re-ran desk-edge, no-ink, PDF-drop and share cases in the browser; full suite, tsc, lint, build

decision: second Opus review: edge flood deleted real ink touching the frame; whitening measured white side bars; 'use as signature' carried across exams
why: fixes from round 1 must be checked too

decision: edge regions count as desk only when they run along half a side or more; other edge-touching ink is kept
why: supersedes the flood-everything row; tail, tight crop and edge word were deleted
evidence: fit.ts inkBounds; 3 new tests failed before, 26 pass after

decision: whitenPaper measures and changes only the drawn image rectangle
why: white bars made paperLevel read 255 so grey paper stayed grey
evidence: render.ts whitenPaper; browser grey-paper case 0.6% grey px

decision: 'use as signature' applies to the exam it was clicked on; shared-image note can be dismissed
why: Opus: choice carried over SSC to RRB without asking

decision: third Opus review: partial-edge shadows, corner shadows and tilted-page desk triangles stretched the ink box
why: round-2 fix only removed regions covering half a side

decision: edge regions are also background when solid (>40% of their box), over 1% of the image and off the centre
why: removes partial shadows and corner triangles while thin edge-touching strokes and tight crops stay
evidence: fit.ts inkBounds; 3 new tests failed before, 29 pass after; browser tilted page and 40% shadow: 0 dark border px

decision: edge-word test now draws strokes instead of a solid block
why: real words are thin strokes; a solid 160x30 block is not handwriting and would read as a shadow
result: noted honestly: test input changed, not the expectation

decision: known limits: ink merged into a full-edge desk is removed (user gets 'no ink found'); 1-px scanner frame 1 px inside the edge; thumb covering >90% of frame; shared photo re-fills the photo slot after an exam switch
why: low impact or pre-existing per Opus round 3; each fails visibly rather than producing a bad green file, except the scanner frame which only enlarges the box

decision: fourth Opus review: solid-off-centre rule dropped bold marker signatures and solid thumbs on one edge; edge-word test sat just under the 0.4 cut-off
why: density alone cannot tell shadow from bold ink

decision: solid-patch rule now needs a corner (two adjacent sides) and one unbroken dark run per row; single-edge partial shadow recorded as test.todo, not a fake pass
why: shadows and desk corners are one run per row, handwriting has paper between strokes; a one-edge shadow vs bold edge ink is genuinely ambiguous
evidence: fit.ts inkBounds runs; Opus cases as 3 tests failed before, 31 pass + 1 todo after

decision: 'Trim to the ink' switch on signature/thumb/declaration slots; error text points to it
why: a heuristic will sometimes guess wrong; the user needs a way out instead of another rule
evidence: render.ts input.trim, studio checkbox; browser: marker corner 35% dark, solid thumb 66%, untrimmed re-render ok

decision: fifth Opus review: run count verified independently; corner rule correct for hard-edged desk corners
why: check the round-4 fix

decision: trim switch resets to on for each new file
why: Opus: an earlier untick carried over to the next file

decision: known limits accepted: solid ink blob in a corner (round initial, thick underline, solid thumb) is trimmed away next to other ink, or errors when alone; noisy soft shadows still stretch the box, same as before
why: user sees the preview and can untick Trim to the ink; Opus judged none worse than a known limit
